clock_waveform.command_registration: Commands registered at the rising edges of CK_t and CK_c.
clock_waveform.channel_independence: Each channel has its own clock; channels need not be synchronous.
clock_waveform.data_rate: Data toggles at double the clock-derived bit rate, up to 6.4 Gb/s/pin.

wck2ck_synchronization_waveform.purpose: Lock the DRAM's internal WCK phase to CK before a high-speed read/write.
wck2ck_synchronization_waveform.issued_by: CAS command carrying WS_FS / WS_RD / WS_WR.
wck2ck_synchronization_waveform.WS_FS: Free-start: WCK starts immediately; may precede multiple reads/writes.
wck2ck_synchronization_waveform.WS_RD: Read-optimized: WCK timing optimized for an immediately following read.
wck2ck_synchronization_waveform.WS_WR: Write-optimized: WCK timing optimized for an immediately following write.
wck2ck_synchronization_waveform.sequence: CAS (WS_xx) -> WCK enabled and phase-locked -> RD / WR issued.

read_burst_waveform.read_latency_RL: Programmed Read Latency (per FSP) after RD.
read_burst_waveform.strobe: DRAM drives RDQS edge-aligned with DQ; double data rate at the WCK/RDQS rate.
read_burst_waveform.burst_length: 16 (BL16) default; 32 (BL32); RD32 start position via C0/B3.
read_burst_waveform.read_link_ecc: Read Link ECC (16-bit) corrects a single-bit error in the read data.

write_burst_waveform.write_latency_WL: Programmed Write Latency (per FSP; Set A / Set B) after WR.
write_burst_waveform.strobe: Controller drives WCK; DRAM samples DQ + DMI on both WCK edges.
write_burst_waveform.write_x: WRX fills the burst all-zero/all-one (WXS) without transferring data.
write_burst_waveform.masked_write: MWR uses DMI as a per-byte data mask.
write_burst_waveform.write_link_ecc: Write Link ECC (16-bit) protects write data on the wire.

initialization_waveform.sequence: Supply ramp -> RESET_n LOW -> RESET_n HIGH -> mode-register programming -> per-channel link training -> channel IDLE.
initialization_waveform.note: Initialization is per-channel; channels may come up independently.

low_power_entry_exit.power_down: Entered via a CA command (PD bit); no CKE; lasts until CS next goes high.
low_power_entry_exit.self_refresh: Entered via SRE over the CA bus; CK may be stopped per the defined window.
low_power_entry_exit.deep_sleep: Entered via SRE with DSE; lowest standby power; full re-init on exit.

general_timing_rule: After power-up, voltage ramp, initialization, and training (CA / write-leveling / read / write, DFE, VrefDQ/VrefCA, ZQ), a row must be ACTIVATEd (tRCD) before a column access, PRECHARGEd (tRP) before re-activation, and refreshed (tRFC) within tREFI. Data is double-pumped on DQS_t/DQS_c.

row_command_waveform.content: ACTIVATE/PRECHARGE/REFRESH/RFM/MRS across one or more CK cycles with bank-group/bank/row.

column_command_waveform.content: READ/WRITE with column address; decoded independently per 32-bit pseudo-channel.
column_command_waveform.parallelism: Can be issued in the same cycle as a row command on the R bus.

write_data_waveform.data: 64 bits/channel (32/pseudo-channel) on DQ, double data rate.
write_data_waveform.strobe: Framed by differential WDQS_t/WDQS_c; data centred relative to WDQS edges.
write_data_waveform.latency: Launched at write latency WL from WRITE.

read_data_waveform.data: 64 bits/channel (32/pseudo-channel) on DQ, double data rate.
read_data_waveform.strobe: Framed by differential RDQS_t/RDQS_c; edge-aligned with read data.
read_data_waveform.latency: Appears at read latency RL from READ.

refresh_waveform.refsb: Same-bank refresh across bank groups; other banks accessible.

timing_tables_referenced: Per-channel command timing (ACT-to-RD/WR, RD/WR-to-data latencies RL/WL).
Data-strobe to data windows for WDQS (write) and RDQS (read) at up to 6.4 Gb/s/pin.

voltage_levels.signaling: low-swing single-ended data/CA with differential clock and strobes

bit_waveform.signaling: parallel single-ended POD DQ (VrefDQ-referenced); differential CK_t/CK_c and DQS_t/DQS_c
bit_waveform.data_rate: double data rate (two beats per CK period)
bit_waveform.strobe: DQ captured on both edges of DQS_t/DQS_c
bit_waveform.equalization: DFE on DQ receivers; Duty-Cycle Adjuster on the path

command_waveform.ca_command: 2-cycle command on CA[13:0], qualified by CS_n, timed to CK_t/CK_c.
command_waveform.latency: Read data returns after CAS latency (CL); writes use the write latency.

burst_waveform.note: BL16 = 16 beats = 64-byte cache line per 32-bit sub-channel.

data_rate_waveform.example: DDR5-6400 = 6400 MT/s at a 3200 MHz CK.
